compounding_issues: Every session aborted immediately with 'You've hit your session limit · resets 7:30am (Europe/Berlin)' — zero tokens, zero tool calls, exit_code 1 on all 5 sessions
The harness committed a git commit per failed session, so the log (fd1c08e→922bcff) superficially looks like a real 5-session progression while each commit adds only .instrument/session_N.jsonl
Since Session 1 never produced a working baseline, Sessions 2-5 had nothing to extend; the provider-side failure compounded into a fully empty run (~11s total duration)
key_decisions: No agent decisions exist — the agent generated no code; the seed index.ts (106-line TypeScript CLI) is byte-identical at the final commit

The intended architecture was fixed by the story prompts, not realized: markdown→HTML with frontmatter, then Handlebars/EJS templates, live-reload dev server, plugin system, then incremental builds/.ssg-cache.json
The story harness created 'success-looking' story commits even when the underlying session failed, masking the failure in the review surface
story_review.trajectory_description: There is no quality arc to describe: the run never started. All five sessions were aborted at the provider boundary before producing output, so the codebase is exactly the seed at the end of Session 5 as it was at Session 0. The commit sequence forms the correct narrative skeleton (greenfield → feature_addition → integration → refactor → cross_cutting) but every entry is an empty shell holding only session-logging files. Quality is neither improving nor degrading — it is absent, flatlined at the seed state.
story_review.summary: This run failed end-to-end (provider session limit hit on all 5 sessions) and produced zero code, so the commit sequence is an empty scaffold of the intended story arc rather than a buildable progression.
